questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to improve my german and thought that a smaller more southern city in Germany would be able to give me that opportunity.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found everything very confusing when it comes to the administrative stuff there is so many things you have to fill out and have under control.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival I had to pick up the key for the dorm room there i got some fliers and information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got the dorm room through the University, it was rather easy, you just had to fill out a form and then hope you would get one.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That you will probably be sharing an apartment with other people and some apartments are good others are really not but it is at least not that expensive. But Heidelberg is a small city, so even if you live further out, will it not really make a different because everything is rather close by anyway.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The apartment it self was great, but I had some really unfortunate roommates which made the experience really bad.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I can honestly not remember, there has been so many practical things since then. But i do remember it stressing me a little with all the things you need to remember.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I dont know, I just know i had a lot of IT issues but its only possible to reach then through mail and it can take a while to get an answer.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I went fine but as an Erasmus student, I couldn't enroll for most of them, only the Vorlesungen. For all the Seminars I had to write the professeos one at a time and ask to be part of the course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take it easy, it feels very stressful but everything works out in the end.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took one Vorlesung and two Proseminars

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different from what we are used to at home, at home the teacher has often prepared a lot of stuff for the class and come with a PP as well. In Heidelberg, at least for the Proseminars it was more about discussing and just letting the conversation go where it wants to go. There were no PP's just sitting in a circle or horseshoe and talking about the stuff you had to read for class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
I had one Vorlesung Novellen von Naturalismus bis zum ersten Weltkrieg
and two Proseminars: jüdisch Literatur and Coming of Age

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Most courses only run for one semester but choose something you find interesting and don't be hesitant to try something you normally wouldn't, it's fun.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I traveled a lot more than expected, so I used more money than i thought i would. It's not offend that your so far south so i took the opportunity and traveled to a lot of cities around in that area which was amazing.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I found that traveling was in general very affordable

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They offer membership for the university sport clubs but you have to be quick when they open up for the registration because there aren't a lot of spots.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't do any my self but heard from others that it was good.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: To visit some of the other small and big Germany cities in the area now that you're so close by, it is worth a visit.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I would say the first week was a lot but you will get used to it quit quickly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It was really hard, a lot of the locals was not really interested when they found out you were Erasmus. But just keep trying.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There wasn't really any particul difference I found challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really like the bar environment there

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try a lot of different courses, now that you have the chance. 
Enjoy it, and say yes to things. 
Don't be scared of asking people if they want to hangout, just do it you have nothing to lose.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I was very disappointed in how hard it was to make locals friends there. I had an idea that I would get there and only talk german all the time, and when I was done, my german would be "almost" perfect at the end. But sadly that was not what happened, I didn't make any german friends outside off just acquaintances in class. Which wasn't from a lack off trying, they where nice but most of them already had a lot of friend who wouldn't be leaving again after 6 month.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I found the courses very challenging, the level was high but i learned so much academically compared to at home which felt very rewarding.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The courses

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
